name: Parv Yadav
feedback: The calm visual design and detailed checklist make a difficult administrative task feel manageable, and completed progress survives reload. Replace realistic prefilled identifiers with clearly labelled examples and date the official guidance; dense legal instructions need a clearer boundary between a checklist and verified advice.
tested: Opened job-loss guide, task details and overview; marked task done, reloaded and confirmed 1/7 and 14% persist.
limitations: No external portal submission, emails, print or legal-content validation.

name: Om Umrania
feedback: Strong project positioning, clear compensation details and a distinctive visual system give Brainchain a coherent identity. Category filtering and project detail pages work; provide a guest builder/founder journey so applications, matching and collaboration can be assessed beyond the login gate.
tested: Home, Projects, Climate filter, project detail, About and login; Climate narrowed six projects to one.
limitations: Application/posting/messaging and persistence gated by authentication.

name: Isha Bhandari
feedback: The guest onboarding is thoughtful and the saved preferences appear correctly in the profile, with consistent property and concierge screens. Make the recommendation logic credible: choosing Reading still surfaced beach shacks and a flea market under a personalised label, and provide a clearly marked demo stay to test service requests safely.
tested: Completed five guest questions; inspected Home/My Stay redirect, Concierge, Profile and Goa property Overview/activities/Ratings; preference values survived reload.
limitations: No bookings, upgrades or concierge messages sent; checked-in service workflow untested.

name: Raghav Saxena
feedback: The dashboard is well organised and the navigation covers a substantial negotiation workflow. However, a synthetic 10-credit negotiation produced an unrelated $165,000 cloud-vendor analysis, and an active deal was labelled executed and verified; replace canned intelligence and audit claims with input-grounded, clearly qualified results.
tested: Opened all seven main sections; ran simulator (79%); analyzed synthetic Blue Company transcript; unrelated Cloud Solutions output persisted after reload.
limitations: No real deal data, communications or external actions; AI/provider implementation not inspected.

name: Prisha Agrawal
feedback: The personal-map concept and visual treatment are appealing, with rich place detail and useful collection groupings. Complete the interaction layer: the Coffee filter and clicked map marker did not visibly change the map, and the new test collection disappeared after reload; also reconcile Mumbai profile copy with Gurugram content.
tested: Map/Coffee/marker, Nearby, Collections, Friends, Plans, Visited, profile and place details; created synthetic collection then reloaded, collection absent.
limitations: No location permission, directions, invitations or real seeded notes changed.

name: Akshat Gupta
feedback: The gallery, timeline and search presentation form a polished, coherent memory product. The core import is still a demonstration: clicking Import Gallery claimed 42,318 memories were processed without selecting any files, while Assistant reported only 40 indexed; make demo boundaries explicit and implement one real import-to-search path.
tested: Visited Search, Gallery, Collections, Timeline, Insights, Assistant, Notifications and Import; unknown search returned 8 fallback memories; import completed without files.
limitations: No personal media uploaded; actual media indexing and AI/private-processing claims unverified.

name: Sukritha
feedback: A thoughtful stall-specific product with a clear sale flow and responsive price, profit and margin calculations. Reconcile the dashboard, insights and sidebar numbers, clearly label simulated scanning, and finish Settings/Product Tour behavior so the operational detail is as reliable as the presentation.
tested: Opened sale and simulated product snap; ₹399 to ₹374 changed profit ₹279 to ₹254 and margin 70% to 68%; inventory, money, insights, copilot, import, badges, Settings and Tour clicked.
limitations: No completed sale, cash transfers, vendor payment or account changes; seeded data untouched, durable writes untested.

name: Shriya Wadhwa
feedback: The heist theme, countdown and keyboard make the game feel cohesive, and failure/replay screens work. Fix the word-length contract before expanding it: the first vault accepted four-letter guesses and displayed four cells, but failure revealed the five-letter answer HEIST; also expose remaining tries and save interrupted progress.
tested: Played six guesses including CRAN/FIRE/DOOM/LUMP/BOLD/SEEK; failure revealed HEIST, 6 guesses and 0/4; replay works; reload returns to briefing.
limitations: Later vaults, coin rewards and tools not reached.

name: Udayan Narain Sinha
feedback: The quiz loop, hint, score and streak updates work, with a clear mobile-style interface. Persist the actual result: my completed run showed 425 points and 40% accuracy, but returning/reloading showed 1,250 and 90%; replace static leaderboard/progress claims with earned state and add explanations for missed answers.
tested: Completed 10 General questions, tested Hint and correct/incorrect scoring; visited leaderboard Weekly and You; result changed on revisit/reload.
limitations: No sharing; online/multiplayer ranking unverified.

name: Akhil Menon
feedback: The opening screen is calm and clear, but Google sign-in blocks the actual mood check-in experience. Provide a guest/demo route and an accessible brief so mood logging, history and follow-up support can be reviewed.
tested: Inspected landing/login screen; only Continue with Google offered; provided Drive brief returned 404.
limitations: No OAuth/login or unseen app screens inspected.

name: Harshit Chebolu
feedback: The deduction loop is solid: searchable Pokémon, attribute comparisons, a clear give-up confirmation and retained guess history all work. Add a compact visual legend beside the logic log and make the round rules prominent so new players understand the direction indicators without leaving play.
tested: Searched/selected Pikachu; submitted guess and saw higher/no-match comparisons; reload retained guess; give-up revealed Crawdaunt; replay and How to Play inspected.
limitations: Winning path not tested; no competitive or account features present in inspected flow.

name: Mansi Hemant Nerkar
feedback: The learning philosophy and graduated hints are well presented, and the app honestly labels its built-in hint engine. Fix the five-question onboarding, which repeatedly fails to load, and ground the full reasoning in the actual numbers: a 100-revenue/70-cost margin example received generic change-analysis advice instead of working through the case.
tested: Tested Think with synthetic margin problem, hint and full reasoning; onboarding and retry both error; journey clicked.
limitations: Onboarding prevents complete learning journey; no external AI connected per UI.

name: Aryan Bang
feedback: The support flow is thoughtful: a relevant AI reply, clear therapist limits, a counsellor directory and accessible SOS navigation work together. Tighten trust claims around verified professionals, encryption and partnerships, and ensure the advertised 22-language experience translates the full interface rather than only its selected-language label.
tested: Skipped language onboarding; tested synthetic breathing prompt and received relevant reply; inspected Counsellors, Tracker, Settings, Language, SOS; Low-data toggle remained checked after reload.
limitations: No therapist booking, emergency communication, location/voice permissions or real mood data; provider verification and language accuracy unverified.

name: Nishita Arora
feedback: A coherent, gentle tracker with an explicit sample mode, useful calendar and pattern views, and saved check-ins that survive reload. Explain the basis and uncertainty behind precise energy and focus percentages so estimated patterns are not mistaken for established personal health predictions.
tested: Sample mode; Today/Cycle/Log/Insights; Ask LUNA returned log-related patterns; check-in saved mood/energy6 and survived reload.
limitations: Only sample data used; no personal medical information, pill/sex actions or clinical validation. Native date-input commit was not verified, so date behavior is not scored.

name: Anjanee Chopra
feedback: The onboarding, timed workout controls and connected fitness sections make this a substantial prototype. Tighten the programme logic: the Push day contains lunges and knee raises, yoga cards carry heavy-load advice, and a new user appears at 40% on the squad board before completing a session.
tested: Completed five-step synthetic assessment; opened all five navigation screens; launched, paused and skipped workout; profile persisted on reload.
limitations: No real workout or medical accuracy assessment; premium and long-term adaptation not exercised.

name: Siddharth Ramadoss
feedback: The sports and esports split, onboarding and match form are clear and thoughtfully structured. Provide a safe populated demo so the central join-to-play loop can be demonstrated; every match feed and history was empty during review.
tested: Synthetic nickname/preferences survived reload; inspected Discover, My Games Joined/Hosted/History, profile and physical/esports post form with required-field validation.
limitations: No games were published or invitations sent; joining and actual multi-user updates could not be verified.

name: Sonia Sharma
feedback: The Indian flower positioning and detailed subscription, gifting and corporate journeys show strong product thought. The next step is to make the operational boundary explicit: seeded delivery tracking, loyalty and subscriptions look live, but fulfilment and account ownership need a clearly labelled demo and an independently testable checkout.
tested: Visited all primary sections; inspected tracking, subscription management, rewards and seeded basket; changed delivery rhythm and spun roulette to a different flower.
limitations: No checkout, order, contact, subscription mutation or real fulfilment tested.

name: Vansh Sharma
feedback: The pixel-art world, responsive narrative and connected quest state make this an engaging working project. Two commands changed the scene, character, stats and quest completion, and Continue restored them after reload; now tighten the state narration, where the journal duplicates week labels and known characters still appear as Unknown.
tested: Inspected Settings, Achievements, Lore, Credits and all eight game panels; created founder, sent two commands, observed progression and reload/Continue persistence.
limitations: Long-run endings, combat balance and alternate branches not exhaustively tested.

name: MOZAMMIL AHMAD
feedback: This is a coherent playable game: clues, hint costs, turn handover and saved scores all worked in the tested round. Clean up the final-result copy—ending early at two points still says “first to 21”—and make the online-room limitation as clear as the strong local-play experience.
tested: Created three local players; drew/rolled, used a hint and correctly answered window for2points; passed turn and reloaded with score/hints intact; opened Scores, Rules and Settings and ended game.
limitations: No remote multi-device room or full21-point match tested.

name: Mehar Arora
feedback: The restrained black-and-yellow introduction communicates the fitness-to-investing idea clearly. Provide a guest sandbox or evaluator credentials so the movement tracking and investment logic can be assessed; the current submission stops at account creation.
tested: Inspected landing, Get started and sign-in/sign-up gate; no guest route offered. Provided Drive brief returned404.
limitations: Authenticated features and financial functionality unseen; no account created or funds action.

name: Dimpy Yadav
feedback: The comparison matrix and saved corridors make a useful commuter interface. Fix the Google Maps failure and clearly distinguish sample estimates from verified live integrations: unlinked accounts already show balances and ratings, while the map claimed an active key before failing and blanking the app.
tested: Visited Compare, Map, Surge, Saved Routes and Linked Accounts; map errored then blanked; reload recovered; selected a different saved corridor and inspected changed fares.
limitations: No login, location permission, provider app launch or ride booking; live fare and account claims unverified.

name: Arnav avi
feedback: The guided planner produces a detailed itinerary and preserves it in My Trips. The constraint handling needs another pass: selecting Solo still produced a “solo group of 2,” a $2,000 budget became an $8,120 plan, and the budget dashboard then showed a different total; reconcile those numbers and make the unfinished concierge state explicit.
tested: Completed five-step Kyoto plan using Solo and$2,000; inspected generated daily plan, budget and My Trips; saved trip survived reload; Concierge remained coming next.
limitations: No bookings or real travel details; discover-destination branch and all activity swaps not exhausted.

name: Anusha PB
feedback: The comic-book identity and searchable council directory give this a clear campus purpose. Searching Anusha found the correct ProdMan profile; now complete the missing portraits/bios and clean up the club taxonomy, where company names and near-duplicate club labels appear alongside actual councils.
tested: Loaded public directory; searched Anusha, opened matching membership profile and contact link, tested ProdMan anchor and inspected admin login.
limitations: No contacts sent, identities independently verified or administrator data changes; content completeness varies between profiles.

name: Shivank Kanitkar
feedback: The sourced company overview, current news feed and persistent bookmarks form a useful research tool, and unavailable data is honestly labelled. Finish the dossier where Leadership and Financials are empty, and replace the repeated interview-answer template with company-specific evidence or a clearer preparation workflow.
tested: Searched Infosys, inspected six dossier tabs and tracked company; news feed loaded dated source links; HDFC filter narrowed articles; saved bookmark survived reload.
limitations: No verification of every article or financial claim; competitor groupings and interview prompts are explicitly heuristic.

name: Akshat Verma
feedback: The recipient questionnaire, detailed gift ideas and persistent planning dossier make a thoughtful gifting workflow. Enforce the budget more clearly—the top recommendation for a ₹1,000 cap cost ₹1,650–₹2,200—and fix the seeded countdowns and profile counts; claims of connected WhatsApp alerts also need to be clearly separated from guest demo data.
tested: Completed four-step synthetic coffee-lover profile; generated relevant suggestions; saved Blue Tokai item into its dossier and verified after reload; inspected Home, Gift Lists, People, Wishlist and Profile.
limitations: No purchases, store-stock verification, messages or real reminders; prices are labelled approximate.

name: Sukhman Jaggi
feedback: The submitted URL currently shows “No Lovable project found at this address,” so the app cannot be fairly assessed. Republish the project and provide a working public link; the accompanying Drive brief was also unavailable to the review account.
tested: Opened supplied deployment; captured missing-project screen; fetched supplied brief and received404.
limitations: App UI and functionality unavailable.

name: Shriraj Deshmukh
feedback: The property-inspection proposition and professional visual treatment are clear. Provide a guest inspection or evaluator login so the defect capture and handover-report workflow can be reviewed; only phone/email authentication is currently accessible.
tested: Inspected phone OTP and email login tabs; no guest route; supplied Drive brief returned404.
limitations: No OTP sent or account created; inspection, booking and reporting features unseen.

name: Shantanu Satish Patil
feedback: The breadth of shop-floor and financial workflows shows substantial domain thinking, and the production filter returned the expected subset. The next pass must make that breadth dependable: the AI assistant fails with an invalid-prompt error, a 13:15–16:20 downtime window is labelled128minutes, and the displayed Works Manager role can still open cash screens outside its stated scope.
tested: Inspected all19 main sections; filtered production120→23Flange records; opened entry control; asked low-stock question and captured provider error.
limitations: No production/financial records changed, communications sent, Tally sync run or legal compliance validated; persistent business writes not verified.

name: Anushka Tyagi
feedback: The bold visual identity and responsive mix controls make the concept easy to understand. Make the audio provenance explicit: an invented song title with no uploaded audio still produced a ready90-second mix, while Library stayed empty and Settings offered nothing to configure; these details leave the experience feeling like an unfinished demo.
tested: Mixed seeded tracks; play counter advanced to8seconds; paused, changed style, visited all four tabs and reloaded; invented title/artist without audio also generated a ready mix.
limitations: No listening-based audio-quality judgment or file-upload/export test; real stem separation and song sourcing unverified.

name: Jaanhvi Mehta
feedback: The restrained burgundy design and consistent Aunty voice make this a distinctive, playable party game. The host/join flow reached a shared final result across two tabs; explain what the final score means and provide a clearer end-of-game recap or replay path.
tested: Hosted room RVXQM, joined as synthetic Demo in a second tab, progressed through20 questions with synchronized answer percentages and commentary, reached Demo score32; host reload returned to landing as the no-save notice promised.
limitations: One participant across two tabs; not tested across separate devices or with a larger room.

name: Hemakshi Mehndiratta
feedback: The campus map, category filters and meetup composer give the social concept a clear identity. Complete the live-map fallback and reconcile Whispers showing a conversation when Active Hangouts is zero; clearly label the seeded profile and demonstrate a real join-to-chat flow.
tested: Inspected Map Radar, Campus Feed, Whispers and Vibe Profile; Study filter changed visible drops; inspected Drop Plan form without publishing; Google Maps Live rendered blank green canvas; reload restored illustrated map.
limitations: No joining, publishing or messages; no location permission granted. Seeded profiles and chat do not establish live multiuser behavior.

name: Harsh Punia
feedback: The craving-rescue flow is thoughtful: intensity, trigger, timed support and a saved outcome feed the dashboard, insights and contextual coach. Separate sample progress from a new quit journey—the app already showed Day1, ₹158 saved and nine cigarettes avoided immediately after setup—and qualify pattern claims drawn from a single log.
tested: Completed six-step synthetic onboarding; logged Boredom craving7→3; timer ran; saved win changed0→1 and persisted after reload; Home/Progress/Coach/Insights/Profile inspected; coach referenced saved amount and trigger.
limitations: Behavioral UI assessed, not medical efficacy; no notification permissions or real personal health information.

name: Prateek Kabra
feedback: The player dossiers, comparison matrix and match log form a useful working analytics core, and the selected comparison survived reload. Improve search ranking so a surname query such as Messi includes Lionel Messi, raise contrast on the small red text, and show the season/date range and provenance behind the aggregated metrics.
tested: Searched Messi then Lionel Messi; opened Messi dossier; compared Messi/Haaland with radar and metric table; comparison retained on reload; Match Log loaded last-five-match breakdowns.
limitations: UI/data retrieval tested, not independent accuracy of92,365-player index, statistics or source claims.

name: Sundram Khorana
feedback: The Delhi NCR positioning and truck-booking entry screen are clear and neatly presented. Provide a guest/demo booking route or evaluator access so vehicle selection, pricing and trip tracking can be assessed beyond the mobile-verification gate.
tested: Opened landing and Get Started; reached mobile-number OTP screen with terms; supplied Drive brief returned404.
limitations: No OTP requested, terms accepted or booking made; functionality and overall unverified.

name: Tanushree Mishra
feedback: The navigation and search interface are clean, and text search returned playable-service links after loading. Finish the product connections: Midnight City opened a Stay detail page, Today retained older history, and disabling ambient listening did not survive saving and reload; clearly distinguish seeded discoveries and Spotify status from verified integrations.
tested: Inspected Home/Search/History/Integrations/Settings/dashboard/match; Yellow Coldplay search returned results; Today filter left Yesterday/older entries; toggle off plus Save Changes reverted on reload; Midnight City card opened Stay.
limitations: Microphone/ambient recognition not tested or permitted; streaming accounts not connected; playback quality and desktop downloads unverified.

name: Aman Sood
feedback: Naggy has a coherent voice, useful planning screens and honest notices about the web limits on alarms and blocking; onboarding and a written review survived reload. Separate seeded history from new-user data and reconcile the dashboard’s nine-day streak and missed workout with a newly created plan; make the coach’s afternoon plan respond to the actual schedule.
tested: Completed seven-step Demo onboarding; all five main tabs plus Alarms/Routines/Reviews/Settings;15-minute Demo reading timer counted down; coach answered afternoon prompt; synthetic review saved and persisted after reload; profile retained.
limitations: No real notifications, alarm changes or seeded task/habit edits; full15-minute completion not tested. One tab interruption recovered; not treated as an app defect.

name: Arihant Bengani
feedback: The spreadsheet-to-dashboard core works: a synthetic CSV produced correctly typed columns, four charts and a matching correlation matrix, and a custom chart could be added. Add an explicit save/export or session-loss warning before reload, and include readable category/value labels on the pie chart so the output can be interpreted without probing it.
tested: Uploaded six-row four-column synthetic CSV; detected date/category/two numeric fields; generated pie/line/bar/correlation charts; added Units-by-Region chart increasing4→5; reload returned to upload screen.
limitations: CSV tested, not large workbooks, multiple sheets, malformed files or data-privacy implementation.

name: Ishita Singh
feedback: This is a clean, focused calculator: platform, format and follower count change the tier and rate output, with invalid counts disabling calculation. Add a transparent rate methodology and engagement/niche inputs, and clear or mark stale results when inputs change; the old50K estimate remained visible after entering−1.
tested: Tested10K Instagram post₹200–1000 versus story₹100–500,50K YouTube story₹625–3125,10K TikTok short-form₹126–630; negative input disabled Calculate but retained prior result; reload reset form.
limitations: Only displayed formula behavior assessed; market-rate accuracy not independently established.

name: Riddhi Gupta
feedback: The case-register theme is distinctive, and rankings, roster search and individual case walls are connected coherently. Provide a consent/removal/reporting path for the publicly named students, clarify why a3–3 case is marked guilty, and demonstrate the authenticated filing/moderation flow with a safe demo account.
tested: Browsed4-case register, both ranking tabs,466-person roster with Riddhi filter returning3, student wall and Case0008; case retained after reload; filing/comments required Masters’ Union Google sign-in.
limitations: Read-only review: no reactions, comments, cases or WhatsApp shares sent; signed-in moderation and consent handling not verified.

name: Devansh Chaturvedi
feedback: The submitted preview is access-restricted, so I could not inspect the storefront or its shopping flow. Submit a published link or grant evaluator access; the accompanying Drive brief was also unavailable.
tested: Opened exact submitted preview; Lovable Access denied; supplied Drive brief fetch returned404.
limitations: No product screens visible; no access request sent; all scores N/V.
